newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria boosts oil products reserves to 72 days.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria boosts oil products reserves to 72 days.

text.p: OPEC member Nigeria which has perennially suffered from fuel shortages now has oil product reserves to last 72 days, Oil Minister Dan Etete said.
Until July this year Nigeria imported large volumes of oil products to avoid a shortfall in domestic supplies when its four refineries were operating erratically.
"For the first time in the history of this country, we now have strategic reserves that will last 72 days," Etete said on state television on Wednesday night.
"We are doing everything humanly possible to end fuel shortages in our country," he added.
Earlier on Wednesday a senior oil ministry official told reporters that the refineries were now operating at 75 percent of their installed capacity.
"Our refineries are improving in operations and the average performance is 75 percent in capacity," said Wilson Dublin-Green, director of petroleum resources.

Poor management and lack of funds to buy spare parts for repairs had reduced production levels at the four refineries to about a third of their combined total capacity of 445,000 barrels per day in the first half of this year.
